thread:
maria (mleng): Heads-up: I dropped the token pack + weights into s3 at s3://redwood-weights/token-pack-phi/v2/ — please use that path for the onboards. config.json is next to the shard files.
allen (infra): Thanks. Can you paste the exact config snippet you expect? I want to validate it against the lint rules before the Dedicated deploy.
maria (mleng): Sure — minimal portion here:
```
{
  "model_name": "phi-compact-v2",
  "weights_path": "s3://redwood-weights/token-pack-phi/v2/weights.pt",
  "tokenizer": {
    "type": "sentencepiece",
    "vocab_files": ["spiece.model"],
    "special_tokens": {"pad": "<|pad|>", "eos": "</s>"}
  },
  "quant": "int8",
  "sequence_cache_kv": true
}
```
zara (serving): Noted. Quick heads-up: tokenizer has a nonstandard pad token mapping — some of our structured-output checks expect "<|pad|>" to be replaced by "<pad>" at serving layer. We should either map it in the tokenizer adapter or update the evals.
sam (pm): Which evals will break? We have the golden-struct regression scheduled for tomorrow.
devin (qa): Likely the structured-output regressions. Our golden prompts assert exact JSON keys, and the tokenizer mismatch can shift tokenization boundaries causing different completions. I can run a small preflight against the gold set now.
leo (research): Also FYI: there are three tokens in the pack that were later merged in training: "▁ll", "▁l", "▁l." — subtle differences. Might affect few-shot prompts where spacing matters. We documented in the tokenizer_notes.md under the S3 path.
maria (mleng): Good catch. I added a mapping table at s3://redwood-weights/token-pack-phi/v2/tokenizer_map.csv — includes pad and merged-token aliases. @allen can infra-bot mount that to the serving container?
infra-bot: mount-request accepted. Mount target: /opt/tokenizers/phi/v2 — status: queued for infra review.
allen (infra): I'll approve the mount but want to run config lint first. @devin — can you ping when you have the preflight logs? I'll block the Dedicated rollout until lint + regressions clear.
devin (qa): Running regtest-runner --preset=golden-struct --weights s3://redwood-weights/token-pack-phi/v2/ --token-map s3://redwood-weights/token-pack-phi/v2/tokenizer_map.csv
devin (qa): quick results: 180/185 prompts matched exactly. 5 failures — mostly key ordering differences and 2 that look like truncated float outputs when tool-calling a calculator.
zara (serving): Truncated floats = tool-caller formatting mismatch. Which tool? calc-service?
devin (qa): Yes, calc-service via our tool schema. The model sometimes returns "3.0" vs "3" and our validator treats them as unequal. I can update the comparator to normalize numeric strings if we want permissive checks.
sam (pm): For rollout, I'd prefer we make comparator tolerant for numeric representations but strict on JSON schema and presence of required keys. That unblocks UX without hiding regressions.
leo (research): Agree. Also the 3 ordering diffs correspond to optional metadata keys we added in the structured call response: "confidence" and "elapsed_ms" — not critical for core outputs.
maria (mleng): Action items I see: (1) infra mounts tokenizer_map (allen), (2) qa updates comparator to normalize numeric strings (devin), (3) serving adapter applies pad token alias mapping if missing (zara), (4) update regen of golden prompts to include optional metadata tolerances (sam/leo).
allen (infra): I'll approve the mount now and run config-lint. Lint command I will run:
```
redwood-config-lint --path s3://redwood-weights/token-pack-phi/v2/config.json --ruleset=serve-2026
```
allen (infra): If lint returns warnings only, we can roll with a canary. If errors, need fixes first.
devin (qa): Comparator change merged to branch qa/normalize-numbers. I pushed a small script:
```
normalize_numbers.py
- converts numeric-like strings to canonical form
- treats 3 and 3.0 as equal
```
devin (qa): I re-ran: now 184/185 pass, 1 remaining failure — a prompt where tokenizer split a date token differently ("2023-05-01" -> tokens inserted). That's the merged-token issue leo flagged.
leo (research): I can patch the tokenizer alias to preserve contiguous date tokens by adding a rule in the sentencepiece postprocessor. Will push to s3 as a small patch by EOD.
zara (serving): I'll implement pad alias in the adapter so the runtime sees <pad> regardless. Also adding a shim to keep metadata key ordering stable in structured outputs (server-side postprocess) to reduce flakiness.
sam (pm): Great. Does this mean we can proceed with a 5% canary on Dedicated after infra mount + lint pass + 1 remaining test resolved?
allen (infra): Yes, plan: mount -> lint -> canary deploy to pool-dedicated-small -> smoke-run regtests with regtest-bot. If smoke is green, we ramp.
regtest-bot: scheduled: golden-struct preflight starting in 15m. Notifying channel when complete.
maria (mleng): I'll keep an eye on the regtest logs and the tokenizer map changes. Ping me if the date-token fix causes tokenization diffs elsewhere.
devin (qa): Will follow up with a summary gist of the failing prompts + minimal repro snippets after the run.
sam (pm): Thanks all. If anything blocks ramp, please @channel and add a short summary here with the failing prompt id.
allen (infra): mounting approved and lint passed with 2 warnings. Ready for canary once the tokenizer alias patch lands.
leo (research): pushed tokenizer alias patch to s3 and tagged v2.1. Tokenizer_map updated.
devin (qa): regtest-bot: preflight complete. All green after patches. 0 failing golden-struct prompts. No tool-call truncation after comparator change.
sam (pm): OK let's start the 5% canary at 22:15 today. Allen, please coordinate the rollout window and monitoring.
allen (infra): CanDo. Rolling canary at 22:15. infra-bot will post status updates.
infra-bot: canary-deploy initiated for phi-compact-v2 on pool-dedicated-small. will report back on health checks.
maria (mleng): Thanks team — great cross-org triage. I'll open the final onboarding PR linking the s3 paths, config, and regression logs.
zara (serving): small follow-up: add note in runbook to prefer comparator normalization for numeric tool outputs going forward. Saves future churn. :+1:
sam (pm): Filing follow-up task in product board. Closing this async loop.
